revision_summary: No deterministic quote failures were found, but the analysis has one foundational issue that needs targeted correction: the transcript's speaker-role tagging is degenerate (every line in the raw transcript body is labeled 'rep,' and the header itself flags roles as inferred 'assigned_from_intro' rather than confidently diarized). Stage 3 builds its entire hostile-to-cooperative customer trajectory, state-change timeline, and rep-intent narrative on turn-by-turn speaker attribution without ever flagging this uncertainty to the reader. On rerun: (1) add an explicit data-quality caveat noting the speaker-role assignment is inferred and may be unreliable, especially around 00:02-00:13 where the opening exchange reads oddly for a confident rep/customer split; (2) soften the 00:27/'tomorrow vs Thursday' ambiguity claim — if the call takes place the day before Thursday, 'tomorrow' correctly resolves with no conflict, so this should be framed as a minor best-practice note (state the literal date) rather than a compounding risk; (3) fix the schema reference at 00:40 — protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number does not match this moment (rep probing a prior no-cost promise, not customer asking how their info was obtained); replace with a note that this is an ungoverned protocol gap; (4) slightly dial back severity language ('compliance exposure,' 'contradictory record') around the 00:55 qualifier-sequencing moment, since the promise and its qualifier are consecutive conversational turns roughly 10 seconds apart, not a scripted violation.
